title: B-Sides & Deep Grooves
desc: Odd origins, stage name secrets & chart weirdness

questions.q: 'Happy Birthday to You' was under copyright until which year — meaning restaurants technically owed royalties for singing it?
questions.a: 2016 — Warner/Chappell collected roughly $2 million a year from it until a court ruling

questions.q: Which instrument did Prince reportedly play on his debut album — and how many of them?
questions.a: All 27 instruments, as well as all vocals

questions.q: The longest officially released song by a major band lasts over 69 minutes. Who recorded it?
questions.a: Bull of Heaven — though for mainstream, The Flaming Lips' '7 Skies H3' runs 24 hours

questions.q: Before she was Lady Gaga, Stefani Germanotta briefly appeared as an extra on which TV show?
questions.a: The Sopranos (Season 3, Episode 9 — in a pool scene)

questions.q: What does the 'AC' and 'DC' in AC/DC actually stand for?
questions.a: Alternating Current / Direct Current — the Young brothers saw it on a sewing machine label

questions.q: Spotify's most-streamed song of all time (as of 2024) is by The Weeknd. What's it called?
Which Beatles album was the first to have no title or band name on the front cover — just a plain white sleeve?
Mozart composed his first symphony at what age?
questions.a: 8 years old (Symphony No. 1 in E-flat major)

questions.q: The vinyl crackle you hear at the start of hip-hop tracks sampled from old records — what causes it?
questions.a: Dust and microscopic scratches in the grooves of the vinyl — it became an aesthetic choice
